operational_rules_learned_the_hard_way: backend `npm run lint` is `eslint --fix` and rewrites source. Gate on `npx eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` instead.
Run backend unit tests as `TZ=UTC npm run test:unit`; some specs count periods against fixtures and flip under other offsets.
Jest here is v30: the flag is `--testPathPatterns` (plural).
Frontend `npm run test` takes ~9 minutes (628 files). Iterate with `npx vitest run <path>`; run the full suite once before pushing.

REDIRECT THE SUITE TO A LOG FILE, do not pipe it through grep. `npm run test > log 2>&1` then grep the log: piping through grep in the command discards the assertion detail, and when something fails you need it and cannot get it back without another 9 minutes. Cost me exactly that.

A FOREGROUND `sleep` IS BLOCKED, and so are chained short sleeps. To wait: start the job with run_in_background, then a second background job `until [ "$(ps aux | grep -c '[v]itest')" -eq 0 ]; do sleep 15; done`, or the Monitor tool with the same until-loop.

NEVER git stash to check a test fails without the fix WHILE a full-suite run is in flight -- the running suite reads the reverted file mid-run. Order: per-file revert checks FIRST, then the full suite, then leave the tree alone.

`git checkout <file>` to undo a revert-check DISCARDS uncommitted work in that file. When the fix is already committed, checkout restores the committed state and silently drops a newer uncommitted edit -- I lost the skipScheduledPayment guard that way and had to re-apply it. Prefer `git stash push -- <file>` + `git stash pop`, or re-verify the file's content afterwards.

A stop hook nags about uncommitted changes every turn, and the suite takes ~9 minutes, so it WILL fire while you wait. Bound the risk cheaply and say so in the commit message (touched suites, consumers' suites, `grep -rn 'toMatchSnapshot' --include=*.test.tsx src | wc -l` is 0 so an added DOM attribute cannot break a snapshot, project-wide tsc) -- but NEVER claim a full-suite result you do not have, and WAIT for the suite when the change is a shared component with many call sites or touches a submit path whose documented precedent is silent data loss.
The coordination worktree is refreshed with `git reset --hard`, which does NOT delete untracked files -- a newly written DEC survives it.
NEVER write a SHA you have not read from git. Use `git rev-parse <short>`.

CHECK A LABEL STRING AGAINST THE CATALOG BEFORE ASSERTING ON IT. `queryByText('Payment Amount')` passes forever against a label that is really 'Payment Amount (required)'; a negative assertion on a nonexistent string is vacuous by construction.
A MOCK THAT DISCARDS AN ARGUMENT CANNOT TEST THAT ARGUMENT (REV-015/031: useNumberFormat mocks were `(amount) => ...`, dropping currencyCode). Mirror the real fallback (`code || default`).

A CHART TEST'S RECHARTS MOCK IS OFTEN `YAxis: () => null, Tooltip: () => null`, so the tick formatter and tooltip content never run. Render their output, and have YAxis pass a tick INDEX second: recharts calls tickFormatter as (value, index), so passing the formatter by reference silently receives 0 as its currency.

FIREEVENT.CLICK ON A DISABLED BUTTON IS A NO-OP, so a 'double click is ignored' test written that way passes regardless. Invoke the hook directly (write it to a sink object inside `useEffect` -- eslint bans reassigning an outer variable during render).

A CONDITIONAL CLICK FOLLOWED BY AN UNCONDITIONAL ASSERTION IS A FLAKE FACTORY: `if (btn) click(btn)` then `expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalled()` fails whenever the element has not rendered. That is the known_flake above. Never write one, and recognise the shape when triaging someone else's failure.

A TEST CAN BE NON-VACUOUS YET STILL NOT FAIL AGAINST THE ORIGINAL CODE (REV-018's re-entry test: the original prevented double-apply BY ACCIDENT by nulling the preview before awaiting). When a revert run does not fail, work out WHY before deleting the test or claiming it as regression coverage.

WHEN A FIX MAKES A DIALOG SURVIVE ITS OWN REQUEST, ENUMERATE EVERY PATH THAT CLEARS ITS STATE. ConfirmDialog wires Modal's onClose to onCancel, so Escape and a backdrop click bypass disabled buttons. Guard the state mutation, not each entry point.

PREFER A REQUIRED PROP when threading a per-entity identity (currency, editing mode): tsc enumerates every unfixed call site. Prefer OPTIONAL with a default for a capability other callers do not need (ConfirmDialog's isBusy, leaving its other 29 sites untouched).

'AN EXISTING TEST ALREADY COVERS THIS' IS A CLAIM ABOUT WHICH BRANCH IT RUNS. DateInput.test.tsx's four 'touch mode' tests all sit under a describe whose beforeEach sets DD/MM/YYYY, so they exercise touch-FORMATTED mode and say nothing about touch-browser.
DateInput has FOUR modes from `getInputMode(dateFormat)`, dateFormat being a USER PREFERENCE. touch-browser has no `if (mode === ...)` branch -- it is the fallback `return` at the end.

AN EXISTING TEST ASSERTING THE BEHAVIOUR A FINDING CALLS A BUG IS A FORK. Does a CLAUDE.md rule or in-repo pattern say which artifact is right? Yes -> replace the test and say so (REV-039's error-swallow test; REV-009's 'does not show loan fields when editing existing LOAN account', whose comment merely restated the condition while MORTGAGE already did the opposite). No -> escalate (REV-017's historical-rate test, whose comment showed deliberate intent).

WHEN YOU ESCALATE HALF A FINDING, set requires_human_approval TRUE and leave it in open/ straight away. Moving it to pending-review with 'reopen if you disagree' works but wastes a review round trip (REV-017).
CHECK THE BACKEND DTO BEFORE ASSUMING A FRONTEND FIX NEEDS AN API CHANGE. REV-010 looked like it needed one; UpdateAccountDto already accepted `string | null` with `@ValidateIf(... !== null)`.
transactions.status is NULLABLE (schema.sql:274). Never `status != 'VOID'`; use the entity's isVoid getter in JS or `(t.status IS NULL OR t.status != 'VOID')` in SQL.
Reuse an existing translated key across namespaces where the copy is identical. A new en-only key costs ~36 parity failures.
A nested withScopedDb JOINS the ambient transaction. There are no QueryRunners left in src/ and lint bans them.
